head: d3411c2196cbb05666ba805a0fc7706028997b93
summary:
Fail. Head d3411c2 adds a large, careful, fail-closed draft of guarded post-merge issue closure. It covers per-issue guard refs, merge and worker guard intents, prepared and per-PR status checkpoints, recovery scan, runner and entry, a merged-context re-review, a policy-adoption recovery path, read-only request history, a rollout inventory and a cutover drain. Its synthetic controls pass (hosted job 40933710494 succeeded). It does not deliver the outcome issue #115 requires.

recovery_entry.verify_rollout still always raises `recovery_rollout_not_verified`. Every guarded path calls it before any write: the native writer main(), adoption_guard.begin, the target-review preflight and recovery_entry.main. No recovery workflow is deployed, and nothing consumes the unguarded AW_POST_MERGE_CHECKPOINT_V1 records. As a result, a linked issue still stays open after an asynchronous native merge, as it did in Core #75, #77 and #79.

Required work that is still missing:
- Hosted asynchronous merge-and-close proof.
- The controlled hosted comparison for the issues:write hypothesis.
- Verified actor and launcher adoption.
- Proof of request ownership, plus safe cancellation.
- Recovery for an admission interrupted before the first status.

The queued-PR liveness defect from the prior review is unchanged at this head: block_unadmitted can permanently block a queued PR whose guard is still held by the run that queued it.

Existing CI, review, protected-branch and failure-to-todo gates are preserved, and no schedule is deployed.

findings.title: Verified post-merge issue closure is still unreachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout unconditionally raises `recovery_rollout_not_verified`. Every guarded entry point calls it before any write: native_merge.main, adoption_guard.begin, policy_adoption_target_review.preflight and recovery_entry.main. No recovery workflow is deployed, and the AW_POST_MERGE_CHECKPOINT_V1 records emitted by the unguarded writer are never consumed. After an asynchronous native merge the linked issue therefore still stays open until a human closes it.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout-evidence verifier. Deploy the recovery workflow through the reviewed policy-adoption path. Then demonstrate automatic closure.

findings.title: Queued PR can be blocked indefinitely by block_unadmitted while its own run holds the guard
findings.detail:
Sequence of the defect:
1. Run A queues a PR, publishes success and keeps the merge guard, because settle and cancel_blocked retain the guard while a request exists.
2. On any later wake, guarded.begin fails for that PR.
3. block_unadmitted sees that the newest Actions status is success and posts pending.
4. No later run can acquire the guard to re-verify and re-publish success, and the request is never cancelled.

The strict required status therefore blocks the merge indefinitely. request_history only observes and does not restore the status.
findings.required_fix: Let the holder of the queued guard re-verify and re-publish success, or bind the request's provenance to the guard so a later run can safely take over or cancel. Add a control for a queued PR followed by a later wake.

findings.title: No real hosted asynchronous merge and automatic-close proof
findings.detail: The issue requires verifying actual cloud behaviour before claiming automatic closure. The only real-provider evidence is the Core #77 fixture, which records a manual close. All controls are synthetic.
findings.required_fix: Run and record a controlled hosted asynchronous native merge in which the mechanism closes the linked issue. Include hosted negative controls.

findings.title: issues:write permission hypothesis not tested
findings.detail: The issue requires a controlled hosted comparison before any production permission change or before native auto-close is treated as reliable. No comparison is recorded.
findings.required_fix: Perform and document the controlled hosted comparison. Keep the exact CI, independent review and ownership gates.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and pre-status recovery remain unimplemented
findings.detail:
Remaining gaps:
- cancel_blocked always retains a queued request, because its provenance cannot be bound to a run.
- Cancellation, and its race with merging, are unimplemented.
- An admission interrupted before the first status has no durable, safe recovery for its pending write.
- rollout_inventory cannot prove that launchers have stopped.
- request_history cannot prove who authored a request.
findings.required_fix: Bind native-request provenance to the guard. Implement safe cancellation and recovery for crashes before the first status. Provide verified evidence of actor and launcher adoption.
